chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from al-Hajjal and Ibn Fazzal, from Thalabah, from Yaqoub ibn Salim, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Whatever aspect may be obscure or dull in the beasts, four characteristics are not obscure to them: knowing that they have a Creator, knowing the seeking of sustenance, knowing the male from the female, and the fear of death.
ai.seo_question: What are the four innate qualities that animals possess despite their dullness?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates four innate faculties (*fitrah*) inherent in all animals, distinguishing them from humans by their lack of moral agency despite possessing these core instincts. This narration underscores the Shia theological view that animals are part of the cosmic order, created with precise biological and spiritual instincts to fulfill their role in creation, yet they are exempt from religious obligations (*taklif*) due to their limited cognitive capacity. The emphasis on recognizing the Creator highlights a universal, intuitive awareness of divinity present even in the animal kingdom, serving as a sign (*ayah*) of God's power for human reflection.
